unit.why: A legend about the Ari, who learns from angels that an unlettered man's broken-hearted prayer of the alphabet ranks above his own; it is quoted from a sefer and followed by a short halakhic note from the compiler.
unit.boundary_note: Ends with a compiler's bracketed note (המאסף) on praying explicitly for one's household; this is not part of the story.

stories.start_quote: שמענו על קה״ק האריז״ל שפ"א התפלל
stories.end_quote: ובאמת קב״ה לא בעי אלא לבא
stories.summary_en: On the Days of Awe the Ari is shown by angels that a simple man in another town prays better than he does; he travels there and learns that the man, who knows only the letters from alef to yod, recited them with a broken heart and asked God to form words and combinations from them.

tags.why: A legend about the Ari, a pre-Hasidic kabbalist, taken from an earlier book.

quotes: והראו לו מה״ש שיש אחד בעיר פלונית
tags.why: Ministering angels show the Ari the simple man.

quotes: והראו לו מה״ש שיש אחד בעיר פלונית
tags.why: The angels communicate a revelation to the Ari.

quotes: והראו לו מה״ש שיש אחד בעיר פלונית שמתפלל יותר בטוב ממנו
tags.why: A heavenly disclosure starts the plot.
Prayer is the subject of the story.
The story is set on the Days of Awe.
The Ari's prayer with kavvanah is implied, set against the simple man's.
The synagogue is the setting of the simple man's prayer.
The man's broken heart and self-effacement are what make his prayer worthy.

quotes: ובאמת קב״ה לא בעי אלא לבא
tags.why: The story's point is the value of sincerity of the heart.

quotes: שיש אחד בעיר פלונית שמתפלל יותר בטוב ממנו
tags.why: An unknown simple man turns out to be spiritually superior; this is borderline.

quotes: ודבוריו פעלו למעלה יותר מתפלת האלהי האר״י ז״ל
tags.why: The worth of the unlearned man's prayer is recognized afterwards.
The Ari travels to the man's town.
